find: I didn’t know him when he’s ashamed.
replace: I had never seen him ashamed.
why: Tense slip (“he’s”); the new line also states what the sentence means (she knew him proud, never ashamed).

find: That night, I took down the copy of the duel poster I had drawn and pinned it on my bedroom wall.
replace: That night, I pinned the copy of the duel poster I had drawn on my bedroom wall.
why: “took down … and pinned it” contradicts itself; FR/ES said she took it down. All three now say she pins it up.

find: “Okay. There are a lot of “worst” parts.”
replace: “Okay. There are a lot of ‘worst’ parts.”
why: Nested quotation marks: inner quotes must be single.

find: His silence changed shape. It wasn’t the locked silence he had kept in front of our parents anymore. It was the silence of a door left open by a crack.
replace: His silence changed shape. The locked silence he had kept in front of our parents was gone. What was left was the silence of a door open by a crack.
why: Removes a stacked “It wasn’t … It was …” pair; same image, plainer syntax.

find: It wasn’t a big, cruel laugh. It was worse. It was an automatic laugh, the same laugh they would have given me if I’d offered to drive a bus instead of Rohan.
replace: It wasn’t a big, cruel laugh. It was worse: the automatic laugh they would have given me if I’d offered to drive a bus instead of Rohan.
why: Merges three short beats into one sentence (FR and ES already read this way).

find: It wasn’t brave yet. It was just fast, hot, and silent, like when you step on a burning stone and run before you can think.
replace: It wasn’t brave yet, just fast and hot and silent, like stepping on a burning stone and running before you can think.
why: One flowing sentence instead of a stacked contrast; keeps the burning-stone image.

find: This is what I should have understood: Rohan wasn’t offering me his place.
replace: I see it now: Rohan wasn’t offering me his place.
why: “This is what I should have understood” is a narrator-announces-the-lesson tic; “I see it now” sounds like a twelve-year-old looking back.

find: I didn’t know yet how useful that sentence was going to be.
why: Removed a foreshadowing tic; the line about “wet paper” works without being told it will matter.

find: That wouldn’t be true. The pain only proved
why: Cuts a redundant denial; the next sentence already says what the pain proved.

find: That’s exactly why my lie mattered. I wasn’t just hiding a project. I was treating her discretion as something she owed me.
replace: That’s why my lie mattered: I wasn’t only hiding a project, I was treating her discretion as something she owed me.
why: One sentence in place of three short, formula-shaped ones.

find: I understood that he was looking for an ending that would let him breathe
replace: He was looking for an ending that would let him breathe
why: Shows Ananya’s reading of Rohan directly instead of announcing that she understood it.

find: The consequences kept rippling away from me like circles on water. Folded up, the stolen square fit in my palm. And yet it reached people whose names I didn’t even know.
replace: The consequences kept spreading. Folded up, the stolen square fit in my palm, and it had still reached people whose names I didn’t even know.
why: Drops the “circles on water” cliché; keeps the detail that the folded square fits in her palm.

find: I had flown under my own name. I had chosen a move. It had worked in front of the same people
replace: I had flown under my own name and chosen my own move, and it had worked in front of the same people
why: Merges a rule-of-three staccato into one longer sentence (the text has very few sentences over 25 words).

find: Everything happened too fast, and yet slowly enough for me to see every detail.
replace: It all happened too fast, and I still saw every detail.
why: Stock “too fast and yet slowly” construction simplified.

find: It wasn’t the stolen kesariya. It didn’t have to prove anything. It was a scrap I was allowed to use
replace: It wasn’t the stolen kesariya, and it didn’t have to prove anything. It was a scrap I was allowed to use
why: Merges the first two beats; keeps the three-part payoff.
Replaces a stock bodily reaction (heart / stomach reactions appear several times) with a concrete one.

replace: The square on his bed suddenly looked a lot more important.
why: Same reason as EN-16; gives her reaction a wry, concrete object.
